title: Trellis MedTech security evidence cookbook and workshop notes
body:
Purpose:
This document collects the security questionnaire answers, mapped evidence, and post-workshop action log for the Trellis MedTech POC. The goal is to provide a compact evidence "cookbook" that the customer security team can use to validate controls, plus an internal runbook for Solutions and Security to produce the artifacts quickly during future POCs.

Context:
- Customer: Trellis MedTech (medical device SaaS) evaluating Redwood Private for on-prem inference of HIPAA PHI-laden transcriptions.
- Engagement: 6-week POC (dedicated on-prem deployment in customer lab), security workshop held 2025-11-04.
- Primary asks from Trellis: encryption at rest and in transit, HSM-based key management, access controls with MFA, audit logging retention 1 year, segmentation of PHI data, and attestation for third-party components.

Summary of deliverables included in this packet (what follows explains where to find each artifact and the minimum acceptance criteria):
1) Control matrix mapping (Control ID -> Redwood artifact location + brief notes)
2) Pre-filled security questionnaire (customer-supplied template) with sources cited
3) Evidence bundle index (file names + short description + hash) for artifacts we uploaded to the shared S3 staging area
4) Workshop notes and decisions (operational constraints, network topology agreed, escalation contacts)
5) Action items and owners with due dates for POC completion

1) Control matrix mapping (high-level)
- ENC-01 (Encryption at rest): Evidence: disk encryption config snapshot (disk-encrypt-2025-11-02.tar.gz), KMS policy export (kms-policy-trellis-20251103.json). Acceptance: LUKS/BitLocker or cloud-disk encryption engaged; keys rotated as per policy.
- ENC-02 (Encryption in transit): Evidence: TLS cert chain export (tls-chain-2025-11-04.pem) and capture of TLS setting (tls-config.txt). Acceptance: TLS 1.2+ with strong ciphers; mTLS between inference nodes and control plane.
- KMS-01 (HSM-backed KMS): Evidence: HSM attestation report (hsm-report-2025-10-28.pdf), KMS integration test logs (kms-integ-logs.txt). Acceptance: Keys are provisioned with HSM protection and private key material never leaves HSM boundary.
- IAM-01 (Access control & MFA): Evidence: IAM policy snapshot (iam-snapshot-2025-11-01.json), audit of privileged users (privileged-user-list.csv). Acceptance: Role-based access, MFA enforced for admin roles.
- LOG-01 (Audit logging & retention): Evidence: sample audit stream export (audit-stream-sample.ndjson), retention policy doc (retention-policy-1yr.md). Acceptance: Immutable logs with retention set to 365 days and verifiable integrity checks.
- NET-01 (Network segmentation): Evidence: network diagram agreed in workshop (network-diagram-trellis.png), firewall rules export (fw-rules-2025-11-05.txt). Acceptance: PHI subnet isolated, only allowed egress for updates and monitoring on specific ports.

2) Pre-filled security questionnaire (high-level notes)
- Q: Where is customer data stored?
  A: PHI data in the POC is stored on customer-managed NFS volume mounted to inference nodes; Redwood control plane does not store PHI. Evidence: mount-config.txt, storage-audit-2025-11-03.csv.
- Q: Who has access to keys?
  A: Customer security team controls HSM root keys; Redwood has a service account with wrapped key access for runtime only; key usage is logged. Evidence: kms-audit-log-sample.ndjson, hsm-policy-summary.txt.
- Q: How do you handle software supply chain attestations?
  A: All third-party components for the POC were scanned using Snyk and our internal SBOM generation; signed build artifacts available. Evidence: sbom-trellis-2025.json, snyk-report-2025-10-30.pdf.

3) Evidence bundle index (uploaded to staging S3 bucket)
- disk-encrypt-2025-11-02.tar.gz — LUKS headers and config dump extracted from nodes (sha256: 0a3f...).
- kms-policy-trellis-20251103.json — KMS policy export referencing HSM providers (sha256: b7c2...).
- hsm-report-2025-10-28.pdf — Manufacturer attestation and firmware hash list (sha256: e3d1...).
- tls-chain-2025-11-04.pem — PEM bundle used for mTLS during POC (sha256: 1f4b...).
- network-diagram-trellis.png — finalized topology from workshop, shows VLANs and jump hosts (sha256: 9a2c...).
- audit-stream-sample.ndjson — anonymized audit events demonstrating log format and retention (sha256: 5d6e...).
- sbom-trellis-2025.json — Software bill of materials for POC deployment (sha256: 8b9f...).
(Full index available in artifact-store/index.csv — request link via S3 staging; interim copies attached to Confluence page CONFLUENCE-3657.)

4) Workshop notes and decisions (items agreed 2025-11-04)
- Network: Trellis infra team will provision isolated VLAN and a bastion host with jumpbox hardened image. Redwood SEs to provide required IPs and ports (listed in fw-rules-2025-11-05.txt).
- Keys: Customer requested HSM; we validated PKCS#11 flow. Action: customer to provision HSM test tokens; Redwood to run integration smoke tests (owner: Daniel Park, due: 2025-11-10).
- Logging: Immutable audit export wired to a customer SIEM; Redwood to supply sample event mappings and a mapping doc to SIEM parsers (owner: Sofia Alvarez, due: 2025-11-12).
- SBOM: Redwood produced deterministic SBOM for the POC image; Trellis requested signed manifest — delivered and uploaded to staging.
- Incident response: Agreed escalation matrix and notification windows. Internal SRE pager rotation documented; contact list attached (contact-list-2025-11-04.md).

5) Action items and owners (short)
- Daniel Park — HSM integration tests + logs (due 2025-11-10).
- Sofia Alvarez — Audit mapping doc + SIEM ingestion example (due 2025-11-12).
- Marcus Vale — Signed SBOM + rebuild with requested sanitizer flags (due 2025-11-09).
- Priya Menon — Collate evidence bundle and hand off S3 staging link to Trellis security (due 2025-11-06).

Acceptance criteria checklist for Trellis sign-off (to be filled by Trellis security):
- Proof that PHI never leaves customer NFS or designated encrypted bucket (checkbox).
- HSM attestation and key usage logs for 72-hour test window (checkbox).
- Successful SIEM ingest of audit events and sample alert (checkbox).
- Network isolation verification via port-scan report (checkbox).

Notes on operational constraints and known gaps:
- We relied on customer-provided NFS for PHI storage; if the customer later requests Redwood-managed storage we will need a formal data processing addendum and revalidation of encryption controls.
- There is a short window where keys were accessed during initial onboarding; logs show usage but Trellis asked for expanded audit context — additional fields will be added to log exports (ETA 2 weeks).
- Backup encryption at rest is performed at the storage layer; we did not instrument application-level column encryption for PII fields during the POC.

How to reproduce the core evidence artifacts (internal runbook)
1) Spin up POC nodes using terraform module PR#482 (link above).
2) Run onboarding playbook: ansible-playbook onboarding.yml -e env=trellis.
3) Run the evidence capture script: scripts/capture_evidence.sh --output staging/ — produces tar.gz and JSON index that maps to the artifact index listed above.
4) Upload artifacts to our S3 staging bucket with restricted ACL and notify customer via secure link.

Appendix A — Quick checklist for auditors (one-pager they can use)
- Verify HSM attestation: check firmware hash in hsm-report against vendor feed.
- Check KMS policy: verify no admin principal outside customer org has unwrapped key permission.
- Confirm logs: compare audit-stream-sample to SIEM ingestion and retention policy.
- Confirm network: review network-diagram and firewall rules, perform external port-scan.

Appendix B — Files attached in Confluence and S3 (request staging link if not provided)
- Index CSV: artifact-store/index.csv
- Contact list: contact-list-2025-11-04.md
- Retention policy: retention-policy-1yr.md

Open questions for Trellis security (to be closed before final sign-off)
- Do they require signed firmware attestation for all inbound VM images beyond the HSM device? (TBD)
- Is one-year log retention sufficient for their internal risk model, or do they want 3 years for certain event categories? (TBD)

Revision history:
- 2025-11-05 (Priya): initial evidence bundle and workshop notes uploaded.
- 2025-11-09 (Marcus): added signed SBOM and sanitizer flags note.
- 2026-01-18 (Priya): updated control mapping and added acceptance checklist after customer security feedback.

If there's anything missing, call out the specific control ID and we will produce the raw artifact or test output within 48 hours.

End of document.
